Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The India Women players make their way out to the middle and spread out to take up their respective fielding spots. Heather Siegers and Phebe Molkenboer are the two openers for Netherlands Women. Kranti Gaud to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Dutch bowlers show character - The nerves did seem to get to the Netherlands Women bowlers early on as they struggled with their lines and leaked 15 wides. Heather Siegers provided the first breakthrough, while Caroline de Lange was the standout performer with figures of 2/32. Myrthe van den Raad and Iris Zwilling also chipped in with a wicket each, and the Dutch did well to pull things back at the death. However, they were left to rue a missed chance when Richa Ghosh was dropped before she added some late damage. It is now a mountain to climb, and the Netherlands batters will need to play with freedom if they are to get close. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Openers set the tone - At the toss, skipper Harmanpreet Kaur said India wanted to be more positive in the Powerplay, and the openers delivered in style. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana took full advantage of some wayward Dutch bowling, adding 59 in the Powerplay and extending their stand to 115 off 83, with both reaching fine fifties. Mandhana went on to make a superb 74 before India suffered a brief wobble, but quick-fire cameos from Richa Ghosh (20* off 8) and Deepti Sharma (10* off 2) ensured they surged past the 200-run mark.

India Women go big with the bat - A commanding batting display from India Women! They have registered their highest-ever first-innings total in Women's T20 World Cup history. The gulf in class between the two sides was evident, and at times the magnitude of the occasion seemed to weigh on the Dutch players. Yet, Netherlands Women deserve credit for their spirit and determination, embracing the challenge with courage and refusing to be overawed. The chase promises to be a steep one, but India have already laid down a massive marker.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Well, that last over was a pretty long one, wasn't it? However, despite all the wides, Myrthe van den Raad only conceded 10 runs, but looking at the bigger picture, India Women will be happy with the Powerplay, scoring at almost 10 runs an over, without losing a wicket. Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities, and it is now time to play. The players of Netherlands Women can be seen in a huddle, getting a final pep talk from their skipper before taking their places on the field. The umpires are also out in the middle and it will be the usual pairing of Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana to open the innings for India Women. Iris Zwilling has the new ball in hand, and she's raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game, but first the flags of the two competing nations are unfurled and the players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Netherlands first, followed by the national anthem of India.

PITCH REPORT - Charles Dagnall is pitchside. He starts by it is a pleasant 20 degrees Celsius to begin with. He further mentions about the ground dimensions, saying that the straight boundary is 62 meters and it is 62 meters and 59 meters on either side of the square. Ian Bishop joins him and says that it has been a brilliant surface for the bowlers, especially with the overhead conditions in play. He brings out the footmarks from the previous game, but reckons that it is overall a good surface for batting as well.

The skipper of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that it is a great opportunity for them to bat first. Adds that it is a bit hard under overcast conditions but they want to test themselves and put up a good total. Kaur mentions that they want to improve in the Powerplay with both bat and ball. Says that they will try to bat with more intent and see if they can pick up a few wickets with the ball. Shares that if the ball starts to move around, it's important to stick to your plans.. Reckons in conditions like this, you cannot start attacking from ball one, you need to spend time at the crease and settle in. Harmanpreet informs that they have made one change, with Arundhati Reddy being rested and Nandni Sharma coming in the team. Says that Netherlands Women are a good side and they are improving with every game. Ends by saying that there is no complancy and they want to focus on playing their best cricket.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says that they will bowl first and hopefully they'll get something out of the wicket. Adds that they are super excited for this opportunity and a little bit nervous as well. The Dutch skipper mentions that it's good to have someone like Sterre Kalis play domestic cricket here and it is actually her home venue and ends by saying that they have made one change to their side.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Yastika Bhatia (In place of Bharti Fulmali), Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Sree Charani, Kranti Gaud, Nandni Sharma (In place of Arundhati Reddy).

Netherlands Women (Playing XI) - Heather Siegers, Phebe Molkenboer, Babette de Leede (C/WK), Sterre Kalis, Robine Rijke, Frederique Overdijk, Iris Zwilling, Myrthe van den Raad (In place of Sanya Khurana), Caroline de Lange, Silver Siegers, Isabel Van Der Woning.
TOSS -  Both the captains are out there in the middle now. Harmanpreet Kaur gives the coin a flip and Babette de Leede calls it right. Netherlands Women have elected to BOWL first.

A look back at the earlier game - In the earlier game, Australia Women completely brushed aside Bangladesh Women to storm to the top of Group A. The Aussies produced a clinical display with the ball, restricting Bangladesh to just 77/8, with Sophie Molineux, Ellyse Perry and Kim Garth picking up two wickets apiece. Chasing a modest target, Georgia Voll made it look like a net session, smashing an unbeaten 45 as Australia romped home with 63 balls to spare. India Women will now be eager to produce an equally emphatic performance and claim top spot in the group.

Fearless Dutch aim to compete - Netherlands Women, meanwhile, can take heart from aspects of their first World Cup outing. Captain Babette de Leede once again stood tall with a fighting half-century, while their bowlers remained disciplined despite defending a modest total. The Dutch may lack India's depth and experience, but they have already shown their resilience and will relish the opportunity to test themselves against one of the tournament heavyweights. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Depth and quality in Blue - India's opening win offered plenty of encouragement. Smriti Mandhana looked back to her fluent best, Richa Ghosh once again provided the late impetus, and Deepti Sharma's five-wicket haul highlighted the variety and quality in the bowling attack. With Harmanpreet Kaur, Shafali Verma and Jemimah Rodrigues still to hit top gear, India possess the kind of depth and experience that can quickly overwhelm opponents.

A contest of contrasts - The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 heads to Headingley in Leeds, where India Women take on Netherlands Women in Match 10. It is a meeting between a side chasing a second world title and another enjoying its first taste of this stage. India arrive with confidence after an emphatic opening victory over Pakistan, while the Netherlands, despite defeat to Bangladesh, showed enough fight to suggest they will not be overawed by the occasion.
... MATCH DAY ...

Can the Dutch spring a surprise? The Women's T20 World Cup moves to Headingley in Leeds, where India Women and Netherlands Women meet in a contest that appears one-sided on paper but carries significant importance for both teams. India arrive on the back of a commanding win over Pakistan, a performance that ticked almost every box and immediately boosted their net run rate in a competitive group. The Netherlands, meanwhile, may have suffered defeat against Bangladesh, but the tournament debutants showed enough fight to suggest they will not simply roll over against the more established sides. With the group stage already beginning to take shape, India will be keen to keep the winning momentum going, while the Dutch will be chasing a statement result that could transform their campaign. Early signs are encouraging - India could hardly have asked for a better start to the tournament. Smriti Mandhana returned to form with a fluent 68, Harmanpreet Kaur anchored the middle overs, and Richa Ghosh provided the late acceleration as India piled up 170 against Pakistan. More encouraging than the runs themselves was the balance of the batting effort, with contributions coming from multiple players rather than relying on a single star. The bowling unit then took over, led by Deepti Sharma's remarkable five-wicket haul and strong support from Sree Charani, as Pakistan were bundled out for 106. Setting high standards - For India, the challenge now is maintaining that standard. Their batting lineup remains one of the deepest in the competition, with Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet and Richa all capable of changing a game in a matter of overs. The spin department, spearheaded by Deepti, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav and Charani, is particularly well suited to English conditions where controlling the middle overs often proves decisive. Valuable lessons from the opener - Netherlands Women may have begun their World Cup journey with a defeat, but there were encouraging signs amidst the disappointment. Captain Babette de Leede produced a fighting half-century and showed exactly why she remains the cornerstone of this batting lineup. However, the lack of substantial support around her prevented the Dutch from pushing beyond a below-par total. A middle-order collapse and an inability to accelerate consistently ultimately left them short of the score they were aiming for. Their bowling attack also showed flashes of promise. Caroline de Lange and Silver Siegers picked up wickets against Bangladesh, while the fielding remained energetic throughout. The biggest challenge for the Dutch heading into this game will be handling India's stronger bowling attack and finding greater consistency with the bat from players around the skipper. The venue factor - Headingley has traditionally been one of England's more balanced venues. Fast bowlers often find movement early on, particularly under cloudy skies, while batters who survive the initial examination are usually rewarded. Spinners can also come into the game as the surface wears, making it a venue where adaptability is often more important than outright aggression. With both teams possessing quality spin options, the middle overs could play a decisive role. Team form (Last 5 completed WT20Is, recent first) - IND-W - WLLWL | NED-W - LLLWL. The bigger picture - India enter the contest as clear favourites and will expect to make it two wins from two. Their batting looks settled, their bowling attack is firing, and confidence is understandably high after the Pakistan victory. The Netherlands, however, have already shown glimpses of their potential and will view this as an opportunity to test themselves against one of the tournament's strongest sides. On paper, the gap between the teams is significant. The challenge for the Dutch is to narrow it. The challenge for India is to ensure there is no room for an upset.
